Q1: Once proximity matching is removed, how should a newly reported finding be tied to an accepted (waived) finding so that it is suppressed?
Choices:
A) Match on the exact `finding_id` only, in both filters. Change the accepted-findings prompt rule (`security_audit.sh:301-303`) so the model must re-emit a still-present accepted defect under its original `finding_id` and never under a new one. Any finding whose ID matches no waiver counts as new and blocks the gate. Keep accepting `SECURITY_AUDIT_WAIVER_LINE_WINDOW` (§10) but stop using it for suppression, and log that. (RECOMMENDED)
B) Add an explicit binding field: the model may set a field such as `accepted_finding_id` on a finding to say it is the same defect as a given waiver. Both filters suppress it only if that waiver exists and has the same `file` and normalized category. A finding without the field, or with a binding that fails those checks, counts as new.
C) Use a deterministic content fingerprint: hash the file, normalized category and a stable defect descriptor (for example the cited function or symbol). Store it on each waiver row and suppress only on an exact fingerprint match. This adds a new state field to `security_pass_waived_findings` and needs a rule for existing waivers that have no fingerprint.
